newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent gives up some gains but still ends firm.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent gives up some gains but still ends firm.

text.p: IPE Brent ended firm but below session highs as profit-taking shaved 29 cents off a technical rally helped by talk of a Nigerian strike and strong products.
April Brent closed 35 cents firmer at $19.47 a barrel, after running into resistance at the session high of $19.76.
"A short-term bounce was on the cards but we managed to get through some important resistance today and now it looks like we're range trading again," said a broker.
News that workers at Nigeria's Department of Petroleum Resources (DPR) were threatening strike action from Friday gave the market a leg-up in late afternoon dealing, brokers said.
The DPR processes export documents for oil shipments. Staff are planning to stop work if their January salaries are not paid by Friday.
"We got off to a good start in London but the Nigerian news gave the market extra drive in the afternoon," said a broker.
Others said a strong performance on refined products markets, particularly gas oil and then NYMEX gasoline, was equally significant for Tuesday's gains.
Shortcovering ahead of tonight's release of latest U.S. oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) was also fuelling the rally, dealers said.
March gas oil closed $2 firmer at $168.75 a tonne.
Analysts said the recent slide in crude prices, which has knocked over $5 off Brent since early January, could continue given a mild northern hemisphere winter and rising Iraqi oil sales.
But Saudi Arabia, the world's largest producer, expects the deline to end once U.S. refineries come out of maintenance and the market starts to focus on spring gasoline demand, Gulf sources said.
